# **Architecture of Graceful Degradation and Failure-Resilient Verification in MuniAudit-AI**

## **Epistemic Abstention and Administrative Due Process**

In public sector infrastructure oversight, algorithmic failure, transient network partitions, or data corruption must never be converted into an affirmative finding of contractor fraud1. Municipal civil works contracts operate within administrative law frameworks where withholding disbursements or initiating punitive enforcement requires legally defensible proof supported by verified evidence1. A municipal verification system that treats an unreadable optical character recognition (OCR) block, an absent telematics ping, or an unreachable vector database as evidence of bad faith violates administrative due process and exposes the municipality to immediate legal challenge1.

When evidence artifacts suffer from physical degradation, transmission loss, or machine learning extraction uncertainty, the automated verification platform operates under epistemic incompleteness3. To prevent false accusations while maintaining operational continuity, MuniAudit-AI implements a formal ternary decision logic:

![][image1]

Under this framework, an adverse audit finding—such as duplicate photographic billing, physical transit impossibility, or weight manipulation—can only be asserted when positive, verifiable evidence demonstrates a breach of physical invariants, statutory rules, or contractual covenants with high statistical confidence1.

If any supporting operational dependency fails, the platform executes a deterministic transition to an explicit abstention state3. The system records an operational deficiency against the inspection pipeline rather than a compliance violation against the contractor2. The transaction is flagged with an administrative status of DATA\_DEFICIENCY\_HOLD or TECHNICAL\_ABSTENTION, which routes the submission to an auditor review queue alongside localized diagnostic context, extracted partial data, and pre-computed repair hypotheses1.

&nbsp;

| Input Data State | Internal Processing Condition | System Execution Status | Resulting Evidentiary Classification | Administrative Audit Action |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Complete & Valid** | Dependencies online; rule invariants evaluated; confidence scores ![][image2]. | Full Execution (Normal Path) | VERIFIED\_COMPLIANT | Automated straight-through processing; invoice line-item cleared for payment. |
| **Complete & Valid** | Dependencies online; deterministic rule or physical invariant fails. | Full Execution (Normal Path) | VERIFIED\_INCONSISTENT | Automated invoice hold; generation of formal fraud dossier with residual metrics1. |
| **Degraded / Noisy** | Faded thermal print; low ML confidence (![][image3]); secondary heuristics applied3. | Degraded Execution (Degraded Path) | INCONCLUSIVE\_DATA | Provisional state recorded; human auditor spot-check required before payment release1. |
| **Corrupt / Severely Truncated** | Corrupted JPEG; unreadable OCR text; negative transit interval. | Component Failure (Failure Path) | TECHNICAL\_ABSTENTION | Technical deficiency recorded; administrative request for re-submission issued2. |
| **Cloud Outage / Dependency Down** | API Gateway timeout; Textract rate limited; RDS pool exhausted6. | Isolated Circuit Open (Failure Path)8 | PIPELINE\_FAULT\_ABSTAIN | Payload buffered to Dead-Letter Queue; automated retry scheduled; zero penalty applied6. |

## **Subsystem-by-Subsystem Operational Path Architectures**

### **Document Intelligence and Thermal Weighbridge OCR Subsystem**

Direct-thermal weighbridge vouchers captured in field environments suffer from severe physical and optical degradation, including chemical dye fading, printhead pin dropouts, grease stains, and mechanical folds9. The document processing architecture extracts critical numeric weights, timestamps, and vehicle registration strings without generating hallucinated characters or fabricating missing digits9.

In the Normal Path, the uploaded voucher image is processed using Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) and Sauvola local adaptive binarization to restore faint text strokes. The preprocessed image is routed to the Amazon Textract AnalyzeDocument Queries API (or a containerized PaddleOCR PP-OCRv4 model), which extracts target fields with character confidence scores exceeding ![][image4]. A spatial token graph associates values with corresponding semantic labels, and a deterministic validation service checks the closed arithmetic mass balance invariant:

![][image5]

If ![][image6] and the vehicle registration matches the authorized municipal fleet database, the voucher is marked as compliant and recorded in the audit database.

In the Degraded Path, which activates when average token confidence falls below ![][image7] or arithmetic validation fails (![][image8]), the subsystem initiates deterministic digit repair hypotheses rather than failing immediately. The system checks whether two of the three weight fields exhibit high confidence (![][image9]) while the third contains low-confidence characters. If so, the corrupted value is calculated algebraically:

![][image10]

If this calculated value matches the low-confidence extracted string under a single-character substitution from known thermal printhead pin-dropout confusion sets (such as '8' \\leftrightarrow '3', '8' \\leftrightarrow '0', or '6' \\leftrightarrow '5'), the platform generates a provisional repair hypothesis. The record is assigned a status of PROVISIONAL\_REPAIR\_CONFIRMATION\_REQUIRED, preserving the original extraction alongside the proposed correction, and is forwarded to the human review console for manual verification.

In the Failure Path, triggered when Amazon Textract times out (![][image11]), returns an HTTP 503 service unavailable error, or encounters an unreadable image (fewer than three recognized numeric tokens), the local circuit breaker trips to an open state6. The transaction is assigned an administrative status of OCR\_UNREADABLE\_DEFICIENCY. The raw image binary is preserved in Amazon S3 with an SHA-256 digest, and an event is published to the audit ledger indicating technical extraction failure11. Under no circumstances is an unreadable scale receipt treated as an arithmetic fraud violation.

In the Manual Fallback, the auditor web console displays the raw receipt image in a split-canvas interface featuring an interactive data-entry mask. As the human reviewer types the corrected values from the physical voucher, client-side scripts recalculate the mass balance equation in real time. Once the invariant is satisfied (![][image6]), the auditor signs off with a structured justification code (such as OVR\_THERMAL\_PIN\_DROPOUT\_VERIFIED), committing the verified values to the permanent ledger1.

### **Computer Vision Copy and Tampering Detection Subsystem**

Field photographs submitted as visual proof of civil works may arrive corrupted, cropped, re-compressed, stripped of metadata, or manipulated to disguise image reuse across contracts.

In the Normal Path, the uploaded photograph passes structural integrity checks, is standardized to ![][image12] resolution, and is processed through an ONNX Runtime container running Meta AI's Self-Supervised Descriptor (SSCD) model with a ResNet-50 backbone. The extracted 512-dimensional vector is ![][image13]\-normalized and queried against an Amazon RDS PostgreSQL pgvector index using Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) cosine search. If the nearest-neighbor normalized similarity score exceeds the candidate retrieval threshold (![][image14]), the candidate pair is routed to a geometric verification engine. SuperPoint extracts structural keypoints, and LightGlue resolves feature correspondences. If the pair exhibits at least 25 spatial inliers under a valid planar homography, the system flags the submission as a confirmed duplicate, records the homography matrix, and highlights overlapping regions.

In the Degraded Path, which activates if EXIF metadata is absent (a common occurrence when field staff transmit photographs through mobile messaging applications), the platform marks the metadata status as METADATA\_UNAVAILABLE and continues verification without penalty. If the primary pgvector database encounters connection pool exhaustion or query latency exceeding ![][image15], the subsystem falls back to an in-memory L1 cache containing embeddings from active contracts, followed by an exact flat scan (IndexFlatIP) scoped strictly to the current contract\_id. If SSCD returns an ambiguous similarity score (![][image16]), the engine deploys multi-crop query expansion, generating five sub-quadrant crops to recover candidate matches that may be obscured within the full frame.

In the Failure Path, if the image file contains corrupted JPEG marker headers or truncated byte streams that fail decoding, the ingestion worker catches the exception, logs a CORRUPT\_MEDIA\_PAYLOAD event, and flags the invoice item as an incomplete submission. If the vector search cluster becomes completely unreachable, the subsystem registers a DUPLICATE\_CHECK\_OFFLINE fault, routes the image vector to an asynchronous indexing queue, and allows dependent validation tasks to proceed without blocking invoice workflow progression.

In the Manual Fallback, unresolved or borderline copy candidates are rendered in an interactive comparison viewer on the auditor console. The interface displays the submitted photograph side-by-side with the retrieved historical candidate, overlaying color-coded correspondence lines between matching visual features. The auditor can verify whether the images share identical physical landmarks or dismiss the pairing as a non-infringing semantic negative, recording the operational rationale into the audit trail1.

### **Geospatial Tracking and Kinematic Reasoning Subsystem**

Validating municipal desilting and aggregate haulage requires confirming that transport vehicles physically operated within contracted drainage reaches, traveled feasible routes to scale houses, and discharged materials within authorized disposal facilities.

In the Normal Path, telematics coordinate streams are sanitized by discarding pings with poor satellite geometry (![][image17]). Surviving points are mapped to the road network using a Valhalla or OSRM Hidden Markov Model (HMM) engine, while PostGIS Linear Referencing System (LRS) functions (ST\_LineLocatePoint) calculate the linear chainage station along the canal centerline. Shortest-path routing establishes the minimum free-flow travel time, and Space-Time Prism analysis confirms that the vehicle moved within physical kinematic bounds (![][image18]).

In the Degraded Path, if the external routing engine fails or times out (![][image19]), the system falls back to calculating great-circle geodesic distances via the Haversine formula, applying an empirical urban tortuosity adjustment (![][image20]):

![][image21]

If scale-house ticketing clocks suffer from suspected drift relative to satellite time, the validation service expands the travel-time window by a calibrated tolerance (![][image22]). If the recorded transit remains feasible under these adjusted bounds, the check is approved with a status of KINEMATIC\_HEURISTIC\_APPLIED. When intermediate GPS pings are lost due to urban canyons or tunnels, the engine evaluates the broader Space-Time Prism boundary between the last known valid coordinates, validating that the vehicle could have completed the transit within physical acceleration limits.

In the Failure Path, if coordinate arrays are entirely absent from the submission, the platform marks the spatial evaluation as GEOSPATIAL\_EVIDENCE\_ABSENT. If device timestamps are corrupt or non-monotonic (![][image23]), the record is flagged as a TIMING\_SEQUENCE\_FAULT. Missing spatial data is recorded as an evidence gap; it is never converted into an automated finding of unauthorized dumping or phantom transport.

In the Manual Fallback, the auditor review interface loads an interactive map rendering the contracted drainage reach buffer, authorized disposal site boundaries, and recorded sensor check-ins. The auditor can review physical driver logbooks, inspect fuel dispatch records, or verify scale-house surveillance footage to reconcile the unmonitored transit window manually1.

### **Cross-Modal Evidence Fusion and Finding Synthesis Subsystem**

The evidence fusion engine consolidates outputs from document extraction, visual verification, and geospatial routing into an auditable case assessment.

In the Normal Path, all extraction and validation workers return valid payloads within configured timeout limits. The fusion engine evaluates deterministic rules, calculates composite confidence scores, logs an immutable event block to the W3C PROV-O ledger, and invokes Amazon Bedrock (Claude 3.5 Haiku) to synthesize an objective administrative summary citing verified facts and calculation residuals10.

In the Degraded Path, if a non-critical subsystem fails or yields low confidence, the fusion engine evaluates surviving rules monotonically. A line-item claim can be cleared for payment if document integrity and spatial bounds are verified, even if the image copy-detection index is temporarily degraded. If Amazon Bedrock encounters API throttling (HTTP 429\) or transient cloud errors, the system bypasses generative text synthesis and populates the audit finding using pre-compiled deterministic string templates that state the observed data and rule results directly10.

In the Failure Path, if internal database operations detect unresolvable schema violations or conflicting state modifications across tables, the system triggers a STATE\_RECONCILIATION\_HALT. An alert is dispatched to system administrators via Amazon SNS, and automated processing for the affected contract is suspended until data integrity can be verified.

In the Manual Fallback, the lead auditor interface displays an unmediated data table presenting raw SQL query outputs, unformatted OCR text, and sensor telemetry logs. The auditor maintains full authority to approve payment, place invoices on administrative hold, or issue formal requests for information without being blocked by automated pipeline exceptions1.

## **Subsystem Execution Paths and Fallback Specifications**

The operational paths across all system components establish explicit, deterministic fallback procedures to ensure that transient infrastructure failures never produce unsubstantiated fraud determinations.

&nbsp;

| Subsystem Component | Normal Path | Degraded Path | Failure Path | Manual Fallback |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Document Intelligence (OCR)** | Textract Queries API; ![][image24]; arithmetic invariant verified (![][image6]). | Deterministic digit repair hypotheses for pin dropouts; local regex parsing. | Circuit breaker trips; record flagged as OCR\_UNREADABLE\_DEFICIENCY; payload sent to DLQ6. | Zoomable split-canvas receipt viewer with real-time arithmetic balancing mask. |
| **Computer Vision Verification** | SSCD 512d extraction; pgvector HNSW search; SuperPoint/LightGlue inliers ![][image25]. | In-memory L1 cache query; exact flat scan on contract\_id; multi-crop expansion. | File flagged as CORRUPT\_MEDIA\_PAYLOAD; background queue for re-indexing; non-blocking bypass. | Side-by-side visual viewer with interactive geometric correspondence vector overlays. |
| **Geospatial & Kinematics** | Valhalla/OSRM HMM map-matching; PostGIS LRS chainage; Space-Time Prism valid. | Haversine distance with urban tortuosity (![][image26]); clock drift margin ![][image27]. | Record flagged as GEOSPATIAL\_EVIDENCE\_ABSENT; non-monotonic logs flagged as SEQUENCE\_FAULT. | Interactive GIS map displaying reach centerline, authorized disposal geofences, and pings. |
| **Evidence Fusion & Reporting** | Bedrock Generative LLM summary10; W3C PROV-O hash-chained event commit11. | Deterministic string template fallback; monotonic evaluation of surviving rules. | STATE\_RECONCILIATION\_HALT; SNS supervisory alert; automated pipeline freeze. | Unmediated data ledger sheet displaying raw database records and invariant residuals. |
| **Ingress & Data Tier** | API Gateway \+ S3 Direct Upload \+ Step Functions \+ Multi-AZ RDS PostgreSQL. | Local SQLite read-cache; pre-signed S3 fallback; Express Step Functions execution. | API Gateway 5xx failover to static maintenance endpoint; DLQ capture8. | Administrative emergency CLI allowing direct database ingestion and ledger export. |

## **Distributed Systems Fault Tolerance Controls**

Distributed systems fail when upstream callers repeatedly retry failing downstream dependencies, creating retry storms that exhaust database connections, compute capacity, and API quotas6. MuniAudit-AI mitigates these risks by implementing distributed systems resilience patterns across all operational layers7.

### **Truncated Exponential Backoff with Full Jitter**

To prevent the thundering herd problem when shared relational databases or third-party cloud APIs recover from transient latency spikes, all retry attempts implement truncated exponential backoff combined with full jitter:

![][image28]

The initial backoff parameter ![][image29] is set to ![][image30], the maximum retry ceiling ![][image31] is capped at ![][image32], and the maximum retry limit is restricted to ![][image33]. If a task fails across three consecutive attempts, execution terminates along that branch and routes the payload to an exception handler, preventing resource exhaustion.

### **Shared Distributed Circuit Breakers**

When external dependencies—such as Amazon Textract or remote routing engines—experience sustained outages, continued retries degrade system performance and waste execution budgets6. The platform implements the Circuit Breaker pattern, maintaining state across distributed workers using an Amazon DynamoDB table or an in-memory Redis key6.

The circuit breaker operates across three operational states6:

In the Closed State, requests route normally to the target dependency while operational faults and network timeouts are monitored over a rolling 10-second window.

If five consecutive failures occur within this window, the breaker trips to the Open State6. All subsequent calls fail fast immediately without making network calls, allowing the caller to execute configured fallback heuristics or record an abstention state5. The circuit remains open for a 30-second cooldown period (![][image34])6.

Following cooldown expiration, the circuit enters the Half-Open State, allowing a single canary request to test the downstream dependency6. If the canary succeeds, failure counters reset and the breaker returns to the Closed State6. If the canary fails or times out, the breaker returns to the Open State for an extended 60-second cooldown6.

### **End-to-End Ingestion Idempotency**

In field operations, intermittent cellular connectivity frequently causes mobile applications to submit identical evidence payloads multiple times. The platform enforces idempotency across all state-mutating API endpoints to prevent duplicate processing, conflicting ledger entries, or multiple invoice charges6.

Every evidence submission must supply a client-generated or derived idempotency key:

![][image35]

The API gateway worker checks this key against an Amazon DynamoDB table configured with strong read consistency6. If an entry exists with a status of PROCESSING, duplicate requests receive an immediate HTTP 409 Conflict or HTTP 202 Accepted response. If an entry exists with a status of COMPLETED, the gateway bypasses backend processing entirely, returning the cached audit record directly to the client.

### **Dead-Letter Queue Topology and Poison-Pill Isolation**

Unparseable file structures, infinite regex loops, and corrupted binary streams can crash processing workers, triggering continuous retry loops that degrade queue throughput.

Every asynchronous processing tier is backed by an Amazon SQS Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ). The primary queue enforces a maximum receive count of ![][image36]. If a message fails processing three times, the SQS redrive policy transfers it into the DLQ. A dedicated isolation service tags the payload as a POISON\_PILL\_DEFECT, archives the raw byte stream in an Amazon S3 quarantine bucket, and posts an alert to the administrative console. The primary worker fleet continues processing subsequent messages without interruption.

### **Monotonic Partial Result Accumulation**

Verification workflows execute as a sequence of modular analytical checks. Rather than aggregating checks into a single rigid block where any individual failure triggers a total transaction rollback, the platform implements a monotonic evidence accumulator.

Results are committed incrementally to an event-sourced audit graph. If the visual copy-detection worker completes successfully, its candidate homography and similarity scores are committed to the case record. If the subsequent weighbridge OCR task encounters a service timeout, the visual verification results remain preserved. The overall case transitions to PARTIAL\_VERIFICATION\_STALLED, maintaining all completed computational progress.

## **Local, Cached, and Offline Fallback Architectures**

Live demonstrations and field deployments often encounter unreliable internet connectivity, cloud service quota exhaustion, API latency spikes, or temporary provider outages3. To ensure high availability, MuniAudit-AI incorporates a self-contained local fallback architecture that maintains system operations without active internet access5.

### **Three-Tier Storage and Execution Fabric**

Data access follows a tiered caching structure that transparently serves verified data when cloud dependencies become unavailable5:

Tier 1 operates as an in-memory Least Recently Used (LRU) cache within the application runtime, storing the 500 most recently accessed scale terminal coordinates, vehicle registrations, and pre-computed visual embeddings. Lookups execute in sub-millisecond time.

Tier 2 provides local container persistence through an embedded SQLite database that mirrors the core relational schema. Pre-computed road network distance matrices for the target municipality, along with contract chainage definitions, reside in local tables. If cloud connectivity is lost, read and write operations route directly to SQLite.

Tier 3 encompasses cloud-native infrastructure, resolving queries against Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (with PostGIS and pgvector), Amazon S3, and Amazon Textract under normal operating conditions7.

### **Standalone Local Demonstration Execution Mode**

For presentation reliability during hackathons and field demonstrations, the platform includes a local execution mode activated via an environment variable (MUNI\_EXECUTION\_MODE=STANDALONE\_OFFLINE):

Image feature extraction transitions from remote cloud services to a local ONNX Runtime engine running an SSCD ResNet-50 model directly on the host CPU, extracting 512-dimensional vectors in under 85 milliseconds.

Vector retrieval switches from pgvector network calls to an in-memory NumPy cosine similarity matrix multiplication across the pre-indexed demonstration dataset.

Document extraction replaces Amazon Textract with an embedded instance of PaddleOCR PP-OCRv4 running under ONNX Runtime, followed by deterministic regex parsing.

Geospatial routing replaces external OSRM or Valhalla network endpoints with an offline Haversine lookup module that uses pre-computed municipal road distance tables.

Audit summary generation replaces Amazon Bedrock with deterministic administrative string templates, compiling the resulting evidence dossier into an on-screen PDF using local ReportLab libraries10.

### **User Interface Degradation Transparency**

The web interface provides visual feedback reflecting the operational health of the underlying pipeline:

When cloud services respond normally, the interface displays green status badges indicating authenticated, cloud-verified execution.

If an external service fails or trips a circuit breaker, the dashboard transitions without crashing: an amber indicator confirms that the system is operating in LOCAL\_RECOVERY\_MODE. The specific degraded component (e.g., "External Routing Unavailable: Geodesic Tortuosity Fallback Engaged") is explicitly identified.

When a document exhibits severe physical degradation or missing fields, the interface renders a structured warning detailing why the system abstained from making an automated fraud determination, demonstrating the platform's procedural due process controls1.

## **Strategic System Directives**

Operating an automated verification platform within municipal governance requires treating system degradation as a standard operational reality rather than an exceptional circumstance4.

First, the architecture enforces a strict boundary between technical operational faults and verified fraud allegations1. An unreadable scale voucher, missing GPS telemetry, or an unresponsive routing service triggers an explicit technical abstention rather than an automated penalty1. This procedural due process safeguard protects the evidentiary integrity of public sector auditing1.

Second, the system isolates component failures using distributed resilience controls: truncated exponential backoff with full jitter, shared circuit breakers to decouple failing dependencies, idempotency keys to absorb duplicate mobile transmissions, and dead-letter queues to quarantine corrupted inputs6.

Third, hackathon demonstration reliability is established through a layered fallback design5. By packaging an embedded SQLite database, a local ONNX Runtime inference engine, and a pre-computed municipal routing matrix directly within the deployment container, the platform guarantees uninterrupted execution regardless of venue connectivity or cloud service status.

Finally, the review interface maintains procedural transparency by exposing degraded execution modes, partial extractions, and repair hypotheses directly to human auditors1. By combining resilient serverless engineering with transparent human oversight, MuniAudit-AI establishes a dependable, legally defensible verification architecture for municipal civil infrastructure governance1.
